text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Portugal is the only country amongst the poorest in the European Union which has clearly lost out with reform to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). It pays out more than it receives, the paper says, quoting a report by the European Commission.
- Economy Minister Augusto Mateus' plan to help companies in difficulty has already saved 9,500 jobs.
- Government gives the Sonae group a December deadline to decide whether to buy failed tourism company Torralta.
- Banco de Fomento & Exterior and Banco Fonsecas & Burnay present the best credit rating amongst Portuguese banks, according to international rating agency IBCA.
- Relations between the European Union and the Portuguese government been soured over the last few weeks by negotiations for the concession of EU funds for the Alqueva dam.
- Retailer companies own brands conquer supermarkets and in six years moved from zero to more than 50 billion escudos in annual sales.

- Employers union CIP-Confederacao da Industria Portuguesa chairman Pedro Ferraz da Costa criticises the government's budget and tax policy in an interview with the paper. Says currenty spending remains too high.
- European Commissioner for the Fisheries Emma Bonino says in an interview that she wants to reduce sardine fishing as a conservation measure but prices should rise to compensate fishermen.
